content.title: About
content.content: Almond butter is a paste made by grinding whole almonds into a smooth, spreadable consistency. It has a mild nutty flavor, creamy texture, and is used as an alternative to butter or other nut spreads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond butter retains nearly all the nutrients found in whole almonds, but in a more concentrated form.
Unlike peanut butter, almond butter is free of peanuts and is suitable for people with peanut allergies.
It is a popular ingredient in vegan cooking as a butter substitute.
There are two main varieties: smooth and crunchy, the latter containing small almond pieces.
Almond butter can be kept at room temperature for up to 6 months, but lasts longer when refrigerated.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support heart health and help regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein and fiber promote satiety and support digestive health.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: People with nut allergies may experience reactions, up to anaphylaxis, from almond butter.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Almond butter is calorie-dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Oxalates can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread almond butter on toast, stir it into smoothies, sauces, baked goods, oatmeal, or yogurt. It also serves as a base for dressings and dessert creams.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store almond butter in a sealed jar in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated, where it stays fresh for up to a year. Discard if it develops a rancid smell or changes color.
